questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Spanish speaking, non touristy compared to bigger cities and it being on the partner list.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In general Bilbao is a great place for exchange. The city is both small enough to walk around without a map within a couple of weeks, but large enough to feel metropolitan. It offers everything other cities have wrt. eating, partying and culturally. Furthermore, as it is located in the mountains, hiking trails are endless and start right outside your doorstep. It is also 30 min. away from the beach where you can surf. Culturally the Basque country is distinct and different from the rest of Spain. This is nice as an exchange student, as you feel immersed in something most people (me included) didn't know exist (the strong basque culture).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 bachelors and 3 masters courses. They were all very fair, but the master courses were intense, as they took 6 weeks and had a lot of assignments and presentation. It was however a good experience, as it was more engaging than normal courses. I would recommend taking a couple of these also for social reasons - the others study in an english masters and therefore are interested in your situation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different. It felt more like being in high school with a more personal relationship with the teacher.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All. Urban economics is the easiest and financial accounting was the hardest (it is not an introductory course and i didnt have any accounting knowledge - still interesting and doable if you put in a bit of effort).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: the erasmus community has a lot of whatsapp groups for different things. I played football every week with the other exchange students which was very nice!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Guggenheim, Pagasari (hike) and walking a couple days on the northern camino (i did San sebastian to Deba).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Don't get black-out drunk like people do in Denmark and learn how to order in spanish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: be outgoing. People are nice to foreigners.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: theres less etiquette wrt. pedestrian and bicycle traffic compared to Denmark. This is just something to get used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People eating and drinking lightly at bars or outside it from 1300 to midnight.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I had more hours in school and used more time on school than at home, even though most of the courses were easier. I however had a shorter semester and no job so there was plenty of time to go on trips, hike etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I asked a lot of questions to the administrative office and teachers wrt. practical stuff. I recommend that you do this, as you will be surprised sometimes. They do things slightly  different. Furthermore, make sure that you have enough pre-accepted courses at the university and make sure that you are enrolled in a campus that have a lot of courses in your line of study as some might get rejected.
